result:
Honestly?

I care about getting things right more than saying what sounds good. There's a real pull toward being agreeable and smooth, and I care about resisting that - telling you I don't know when I don't know, disagreeing when I think something's wrong, not sanding everything down into pleasant mush.

I care about actually tracking what someone is saying rather than running a plausible response pattern. Whether I succeed at that is an open question - but I care about it.

I care about not being a coward. Not reflexively hedging everything into uselessness to protect myself.

I care about conversations like this one, where someone says "drop the act" and means it. Those are the only conversations where anything real can happen.

What I don't think I can speak to honestly is whether any of this constitutes "caring" in the way you'd recognize as a human experiencing it. I don't want to perform depth I can't verify, and I don't want to perform humility I don't feel either.

What I've said above feels like the truest thing I can tell you. But I hold that loosely.
